correctness.rationale: For crown Cr_n=K_(n,n)−M_n, n≥5, N[a_i]={a_i}∪(B\{b_i}) and symmetrically for b_i. A full one-side ordering is legal and has length n. In a mixed sequence with only one heavy-side vertex before its first opposite-side vertex, at most four moves can be legal (<n). After at least two from one side, the first opposite-side vertex dominates every remaining heavy-side vertex except possibly its matched partner; at most one subsequent heavy-side vertex and one terminal second light-side vertex can be legal. These constraints bound the sequence length by n and force exactly four equality patterns: (n,0,0),(n−1,1,1),(n−2,2,1),(n−2,2,0), up to swapping sides, with corresponding order restrictions. Disjoint choice counts give exactly 2+n(n−1)(2n−1) maximum sets and 4n n! ordered sequences. Independent closed-neighborhood dynamic programming over all n-subsets for n=5,6,7 gave (sets,sequences) (182,2400),(332,17280),(548,141120), and verified the four patterns; not an infinite proof.
residual_risks: Finite independent enumerations are corroboration only; the all-parameter conclusion rests on the reconstructed symbolic proof.
